nodes.summary: For every finite group $K$ there are a finite group $G$ and a surjective homomorphism $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \to K$ whose kernel is the group $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ of inner automorphisms of $G$; equivalently, $\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G) / \mathrm{Inn}(G)$ is isomorphic to $K$. That is, the answer to Kourovka Problem 16.59 is positive.
nodes.title: Every finite group is the outer automorphism group of a finite group

nodes.summary: The statement that for every finite group $K$ there are a finite group $G$ and a surjective homomorphism $\mathrm{Aut}(G) \to K$ whose kernel is the group $\mathrm{Inn}(G)$ of inner automorphisms of $G$, that is, $K$ is isomorphic to $\mathrm{Out}(G) = \mathrm{Aut}(G) / \mathrm{Inn}(G)$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 16.59 (finite groups as outer automorphism groups)

nodes.summary: For every group $G$ there is a metabelian group $M$ (one whose second derived subgroup $M''$ is trivial) with trivial centre such that the outer automorphism group $\operatorname{Out}(M) = \operatorname{Aut}(M)/\operatorname{Inn}(M)$ is isomorphic to $G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 11.26 (Göbel) in the negative (Göbel and Paras).
nodes.title: Every group is the outer automorphism group of a centreless metabelian group

nodes.summary: The statement (Kourovka Problem 11.26, Göbel) that there is a group $G$ such that for every metabelian group $M$ (one whose second derived subgroup $M''$ is trivial) with trivial centre, the outer automorphism group $\operatorname{Out}(M)$ is not isomorphic to $G$.
nodes.title: A group that is not an outer automorphism group of a centreless metabelian group

nodes.summary: For groups $M$ and $G$, the statement that $\operatorname{Out}(M) \cong G$, expressed without forming the quotient: there is a surjective homomorphism $\operatorname{Aut}(M) \to G$ whose kernel is exactly the inner automorphism group $\operatorname{Inn}(M)$, the image of the conjugation map $M \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$.
nodes.title: Outer automorphism group isomorphic to a given group
